newsitem.title: GERMANY: German budget freeze not ruled out next weeks-Bonn.
newsitem.headline: German budget freeze not ruled out next weeks-Bonn.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel is not ruling out the possibility of a freeze on his 1997 budget in the next few weeks, a ministry spokesman said on Saturday.
But a final decision has not been made, he told Reuters in response to a query about a report in German magazine Focus, that Waigel planned to take the step in the coming week.

The news came after weeks of speculation over whether Waigel would freeze the budget -- a move that, according to the Focus report which was released ahead of publication on Monday, could save three billion marks.
The spokesman declined say how much a freeze might save.
If the freeze goes ahead, additional spending over a certain amount would have to be personally authorised by Waigel.
